title: Signal Bleed — Dadich Duotone Feature
description: A Wired-era tech-culture feature opener where a geometric display-sans headline bleeds past the duotone hero image edge, anchored by an italic serif subhead and a high-contrast section chip — the deliberately loud, opinionated Dadich grid, not a polished corporate one.
philosophy: This template exists to manufacture productive tension: the headline crashing across the photographic frame is structural argument, not decorative flair. It rejects equidistant margins, tasteful breathing room, and centrist layout neutrality. The duotone image strips photography down to pure concept, eliminating color credibility so the idea carries all the weight. It is built for the moment when a single thesis needs to land before the speaker utters a word.
goodFor: single bold thesis or 3-line pull-quote hero moments
branded editorial or journalism-style pitch decks
conference keynote feature slides built around one striking image
avoidFor: investor decks requiring calm authoritative restraint
multi-column reference or dense academic content
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a magazine feature page forcibly broken open: the headline crashes through the duotone image boundary as structural argument, not decoration. The duotone reduces photography to pure signal — two tones, raw idea, all warmth stripped away. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric and deliberately unresolved, the aggressive overprint held in tension with a single quiet italic line below it. Avoid symmetry, equidistant margins, and any trace of corporate equanimity — every element must feel placed with editorial conviction.

examples.layoutNotes: Asymmetric 12-column grid; the duotone hero image bleeds to the top, right, and bottom edges, occupying roughly the right two-thirds of the slide field. The display headline originates in the left column band but physically overprints the image boundary — no respectful margin, type crossing into the photograph as a deliberate structural act. A compact section chip (category label or deck series tag) is pinned to the upper-left outside the image frame, the sole fully contained element on the slide. The italic serif subhead lands directly beneath the headline crash zone, indented one column from the left edge, separated from the headline mass by a single thin rule rather than white space.

examples.promptCore: A tech-culture editorial spread caught mid-argument — built for the moment one idea must land before any explanation arrives. The duotone image reads as pure concept backdrop, stripped of color credibility, with the main statement colliding across its boundary rather than sitting politely beside it. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric and confrontational: the text zone crowds left while the image bleeds right, the overlap itself being the structural argument. Avoid symmetry, tasteful breathing room, corporate softness, or any visual cadence that signals an orderly list of points.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with deliberate imbalance: the primary text block occupies cols 1–7 with a tight left margin (~4%), while a duotone image panel bleeds from col 6 to the right edge, producing a forced structural overlap zone. A high-contrast section chip anchors the top-left as a categorical label, sitting outside the content hierarchy. The main content element — a pull-quote, bold stat callout, or 3-line thesis — renders in display-sans and intentionally crosses the image boundary line as a load-bearing compositional act. An italic serif secondary line or attribution follows below at reduced scale; page number is pinned bottom-right.
